lessonGoal: Students will read an informational explanation text about SIM cards, identify the main idea and supporting details, learn technology vocabulary, and write short explanatory responses about how phones connect to mobile networks.

warmUp.title: Warm-up
warmUp.instructions: Think about mobile phones, networks, and technology. Answer the warm-up questions below. There are no right or wrong answers.
questions: What do you usually use your phone for?
What happens when your phone has no Wi-Fi?
Have you ever heard of a SIM card or eSIM? What do you think it does?

article.title: What’s a SIM Card?
article.source: Source: Adapted from teacher-provided classroom source image.
paragraphs: When you use a smartphone, you can call friends, send messages, and browse the internet almost anywhere. But have you ever wondered how your phone knows which mobile network to connect to? The answer is a tiny chip called a SIM card. SIM stands for Subscriber Identity Module. A SIM card is like a phone's digital name tag or bus pass. Just as a student ID shows who you are at school, a SIM card contains special information that identifies your phone and your account to your phone company. Without a SIM card, your phone would not know who you are or which network to join.

The history of SIM cards began in 1991. The first SIM card was created by a German technology company named Giesecke+Devrient for Radiolinja, a mobile operator in Finland that launched one of the world's first digital mobile networks. In those early days, mobile phones were big and bulky, and the first SIM cards were as large as credit cards! However, SIM cards made mobile phones much more flexible. For the first time, users could move their personal phone number and network subscription from one device to another simply by swapping the small card.

Inside every SIM card is a tiny computer chip that stores a unique identification number. How does it work when you turn on your phone? First, when you put a SIM card into your device and turn it on, the card communicates with a nearby mobile network tower. Next, the SIM card sends its special ID number to the network, essentially saying, 'Hey, it's me!' Then, the network verifies your account information, including your phone number and data plan. Finally, once the network approves your ID, your phone is ready to make calls, send text messages, and go online when Wi-Fi is unavailable.

Over the past three decades, SIM cards have evolved dramatically. As mobile devices became slimmer, physical SIM cards shrank from credit-card size to mini SIMs, micro SIMs, and nano SIMs. Today, many modern smartphones use an eSIM, or embedded SIM, which is built directly inside the phone's circuit board. With an eSIM, users can download their network information digitally and switch mobile plans without swapping a physical plastic card. Today, billions of SIM cards are active around the world, connecting not only smartphones, but also smartwatches, tablets, and even connected cars to mobile networks.

B. SIM cards are only used for Wi-Fi at home.
C. The first SIM card was created for smartwatches and cars.
D. Phones do not need SIM cards or eSIMs to connect to mobile networks.

languageFocus.title: Language Focus
languageFocus.explanation: In process explanation texts, writers use sequential connectors (first, next, then, after that, finally) and functional expressions (helps your phone, is used to, without it) to explain step-by-step procedures and system functions clearly.
examples: First, when you put a SIM card into your phone, the device reads the chip.
Next, the SIM card sends its special ID number to the mobile network.
Then, the network checks your account information and plan.
After that, your phone can make calls, send texts, and go online.
A SIM card helps your phone connect to a mobile network when Wi-Fi is unavailable.
A microchip is used to store your unique ID number.
Without a SIM card, your phone would not know which network to join.

writingPractice.title: Writing Practice
writingPractice.description: Write short responses to the questions below. Use 2–4 complete sentences for each response.

prompts.question: Why is a SIM card important for a mobile phone?
prompts.modelAnswer: A SIM card is important because it holds the user's phone number and account details. It allows the phone to identify itself to a mobile network so the user can make calls, send texts, and use cellular internet. Without a SIM card, a smartphone cannot access mobile network services.
prompts.compareTip: Did your answer explain that a SIM card holds user info and allows a phone to connect to mobile networks for calls, texts, and data?

prompts.question: How is a SIM card like a name tag or bus pass?
prompts.modelAnswer: A SIM card is like a name tag or bus pass because it identifies the phone and user to the mobile network. Just as a bus pass proves you have permission to ride, a SIM card sends a special ID number to prove you have an active account with the phone company.
prompts.compareTip: Did your answer mention that it identifies the user and proves permission/account access to the network?

prompts.question: What happens after a phone reads the SIM card?
prompts.modelAnswer: After a phone reads the SIM card, the card transmits its unique ID number to the nearest mobile network tower. Next, the network verifies the user's account details, phone number, and plan. Once verified, the network grants full access for calling, texting, and mobile data.
prompts.compareTip: Did your answer mention transmitting an ID number and verifying account details/plans?

prompts.question: Why might eSIMs be more convenient than physical SIM cards?
prompts.modelAnswer: eSIMs are more convenient because they are built directly inside the phone's circuit board. Users can activate network plans digitally without waiting for a physical plastic card to arrive or swapping small chips with tiny tools. It also makes switching mobile carriers much faster and easier.
prompts.compareTip: Did your answer mention digital plan downloads or avoiding physical card swapping?

writingTask.title: Writing Task
writingTask.prompt: Write a short process explanation paragraph of 100–140 words answering this question: How does a SIM card help a phone connect to a mobile network?
checklist: Explain what a SIM card is.
Describe the process step by step.
Use at least two details from the article.
Use process language such as first, next, then, when, after that, or finally.
Explain why SIM cards or eSIMs are useful.
End with a clear concluding sentence.
writingTask.modelAnswer: A SIM card helps a phone connect to a mobile network by identifying the user. A SIM card is a small chip that goes inside a phone and holds a special ID number. First, when you put the SIM card into the phone and turn it on, the phone reads the card. Next, the SIM card tells the mobile network who the user is. Then, the network checks the account information, such as the phone number and plan. After that, the phone can make calls, send texts, and go online. SIM cards are useful because they let people move their number from one phone to another. Today, eSIMs make this even easier because users can connect digitally without swapping a physical card.

teacherNotes: Explain SIM cards with simple analogies: name tag, bus pass, or student ID card.
Emphasize that a SIM card identifies the user to the network.
Help students understand the process step by step.
Compare physical SIM cards and eSIMs.
For lower-level students, provide sentence frames.
For stronger students, ask them to explain how eSIMs might change phone use in the future.

teachingScript.actions: Welcome students and write 'HOW PHONES CONNECT' on the board. Ask students: What do you use your phone for? What happens when Wi-Fi is turned off? Introduce the analogy of a student ID card or bus pass: just as a bus pass lets you board a bus, a SIM card grants your phone access to a mobile network tower. Discuss student familiarity with physical SIMs versus eSIMs.

Pre-teach key vocabulary: SIM card, Subscriber Identity Module, mobile network, device, chip, ID number, account information, flexible, and eSIM. Break down 'Subscriber Identity Module' word by word so students understand that 'subscriber' means user, 'identity' means who you are, and 'module' means component.

Instruct students to read the article silently once for main ideas. Ask gist questions: What is a SIM card? How has SIM technology evolved over time? Have students complete the Main Idea MCQ independently, then confirm why Option A is correct.

teachingScript.phase: Second reading for detail and evidence
teachingScript.actions: Read the passage aloud or call on student volunteers paragraph by paragraph. Highlight key historical facts (1991, Giesecke+Devrient, Radiolinja) and the 4 step connection process (reading card, sending ID, verifying plan, activating calls/data). Have students complete Reading Comprehension MCQs and Evidence from the Text using 'Check & Compare'.

Explicitly teach process explanation connectors: 'first', 'next', 'then', 'after that', 'finally', and functional phrases: 'helps your phone', 'is used to', and 'without it'. Model how to sequence steps clearly. Guide students through the sentence completion items.

Direct students to complete the 4 short written-response questions in 2–4 complete sentences each. Walk around to provide individual feedback. Prompt students to click 'Check & Compare' to evaluate their responses against the model answers.

Introduce the final prompt: 'How does a SIM card help a phone connect to a mobile network?' Review the checklist requirements: 100–140 words, definition, step-by-step process, sequential connectors (first, next, then, after that), text details, usefulness of SIMs/eSIMs, and a concluding sentence.

Guide students through the Self-check checklist. Instruct them to enter their Name and Student Code, then click 'Submit Lesson'. Point out that submitting reveals the full model answer for self-reflection.

sentences.naturalKorean: SIM 카드는 스마트폰의 디지털 명찰이나 버스 승차권과 같습니다.

mustKnowChunks.use: 전치사 like를 사용하여 비유나 비유적 직유를 표현합니다.
mustKnowChunks.example: The smartphone is like a pocket computer.

mustKnowChunks.use: 신원을 확인해주는 디지털 표식을 뜻합니다.
mustKnowChunks.example: Your profile is like a digital name tag.

sentences.mustKnowGrammar: 전치사 'like'가 쓰여 'A SIM card'를 'digital name tag'와 'bus pass'에 직유법으로 비유하고 있습니다.
sentences.feynmanExplanation: 학생증이 없으면 학교 도서관에 못 들어가듯, SIM 카드는 핸드폰이 통신사라는 문을 통과하게 해주는 승차권이자 명찰이에요.

teachingTranscript.english: Notice the student-friendly analogy: 'name tag or bus pass'.
teachingTranscript.korean: 이해하기 쉬운 비유 표현에 주목하세요: '명찰 또는 버스 승차권'.

sentences.original: Just as a student ID shows who you are at school, a SIM card contains special information that identifies your phone and your account to your phone company.
sentences.chunkReading: Just as a student ID shows / who you are at school, / a SIM card contains / special information / that identifies your phone and your account / to your phone company.
sentences.directKorean: 학생증이 보여주는 것처럼 / 학교에서 당신이 누구인지를, / SIM 카드는 포함한다 / 특별한 정보를 / 당신의 전화기와 계정을 식별해 주는 / 당신의 통신사에.
sentences.naturalKorean: 학생증이 학교에서 여러분이 누구인지를 보여주듯, SIM 카드는 통신사에 여러분의 스마트폰과 계정을 식별해 주는 특별한 정보를 담고 있습니다.

mustKnowChunks.use: 양태 접속사로 앞뒤 상황의 유사성을 비유할 때 사용합니다.
mustKnowChunks.example: Just as water flows down, energy changes form.

mustKnowChunks.use: identify A to B 구문으로 A의 신원을 B에게 확인시켜 줌을 뜻합니다.
mustKnowChunks.example: The serial number identifies your device to support.

sentences.mustKnowGrammar: 접속사 'Just as'절이 앞서며, 주절에서는 관계대명사 주격 'that'이 'special information'을 수식합니다.
sentences.feynmanExplanation: 학생증에 이름과 학번이 적혀있듯, SIM 카드 속에는 통신사가 내 핸드폰 번호와 요금제를 알아볼 수 있는 암호 정보가 들어있답니다.

teachingTranscript.english: 'Just as...' forms a clear comparative analogy.
teachingTranscript.korean: 'Just as...' 구문이 명확한 비교 비유를 형성합니다.

sentences.original: Without a SIM card, your phone would not know who you are or which network to join.
sentences.chunkReading: Without a SIM card, / your phone would not know / who you are / or which network to join.
sentences.directKorean: SIM 카드가 없다면, / 당신의 전화기는 알지 못할 것이다 / 당신이 누구인지 / 또는 어떤 네트워크에 참여해야 할지를.
sentences.naturalKorean: SIM 카드가 없다면 여러분의 스마트폰은 여러분이 누구인지, 혹은 어떤 네트워크에 접속해야 할지 알 수 없을 것입니다.

mustKnowChunks.use: 가정법을 이끄는 전치사구로 반대 상황을 가정한 표현입니다.
mustKnowChunks.example: Without a map, we would get lost.

mustKnowChunks.use: 의문사 + to부정사 구문입니다.
mustKnowChunks.example: They wondered which team to join.

sentences.mustKnowGrammar: 전치사구 'Without...'가 가정법 과거 구문(would not know)의 조건을 형성하며, 'who you are'와 'which network to join'이 병렬 목적어로 연결됩니다.
sentences.feynmanExplanation: SIM 카드가 없으면 핸드폰은 자기가 어느 통신사 손님인지 몰라 먹통이 되어 버려요.

teachingTranscript.english: Notice the conditional mood: 'would not know'.
teachingTranscript.korean: 가정법 어조 'would not know'를 확인하세요.

sentences.original: The history of SIM cards began in 1991.
sentences.chunkReading: The history of SIM cards / began in 1991.
sentences.directKorean: SIM 카드의 역사는 / 1991년에 시작되었다.
sentences.naturalKorean: SIM 카드의 역사는 1991년에 시작되었습니다.

mustKnowChunks.use: 어떤 기술이나 분야의 기원을 설명할 때 씁니다.
mustKnowChunks.example: The history of computers spans centuries.

sentences.mustKnowGrammar: 단순 과거 시제 동사 'began'과 연도 전치사구 'in 1991'이 쓰였습니다.
sentences.feynmanExplanation: SIM 카드가 처음 세상에 나온 것은 1991년, 지금으로부터 30여 년 전 일이에요.

teachingTranscript.english: It introduces the historical timeline section.
teachingTranscript.korean: 역사적 타임라인 단락의 시작을 알려줍니다.

sentences.original: The first SIM card was created by a German technology company named Giesecke+Devrient for Radiolinja, a mobile operator in Finland that launched one of the world's first digital mobile networks.
sentences.chunkReading: The first SIM card / was created by a German technology company / named Giesecke+Devrient / for Radiolinja, / a mobile operator in Finland / that launched one of the world's first digital mobile networks.
sentences.directKorean: 최초의 SIM 카드는 / 독일의 기술 회사에 의해 만들어졌다 / Giesecke+Devrient라 불리는 / 라디오린야를 위해, / 핀란드의 이동 통신사인 / 세계 최초의 디지털 이동 통신망 중 하나를 개설한.
sentences.naturalKorean: 최초의 SIM 카드는 세계 최초의 디지털 이동 통신망 중 하나를 구축한 핀란드의 이동 통신사 Radiolinja를 위해 독일 기술 회사인 Giesecke+Devrient가 제작했습니다.

mustKnowChunks.use: 과거 수동태 구문으로 발명 주체를 나타냅니다.
mustKnowChunks.example: The software was created by a team of engineers.

mustKnowChunks.use: one of the + 최상급 + 복수명사 구문입니다.
mustKnowChunks.example: This was one of the world's first digital networks.

sentences.mustKnowGrammar: 수동태 구문(was created by), 과거분사 수식어(named...), 동격 설명구(a mobile operator...), 그리고 주격 관계대명사절(that launched...)이 겹쳐진 복합문 구조입니다.
sentences.feynmanExplanation: 독일 회사(Giesecke+Devrient)가 만들어 핀란드의 통신사(Radiolinja)에 공급한 것이 세계 최초의 SIM 카드였어요.

teachingTranscript.english: Notice the multiple clauses building historical detail.
teachingTranscript.korean: 역사적 상세 정보를 구축하는 여러 절들을 확인하세요.

sentences.original: In those early days, mobile phones were big and bulky, and the first SIM cards were as large as credit cards!
sentences.chunkReading: In those early days, / mobile phones were big and bulky, / and the first SIM cards / were as large as credit cards!
sentences.directKorean: 그 초창기 시절에, / 휴대전화는 크고 둔중했다, / 그리고 최초의 SIM 카드들은 / 신용카드만큼 컸다!
sentences.naturalKorean: 그 시절 초창기 휴대전화는 매우 크고 투박했으며, 최초의 SIM 카드는 무려 신용카드 크기만큼 컸습니다!

mustKnowChunks.use: 과거 초기 단계를 설명할 때 사용합니다.
mustKnowChunks.example: In those early days, internet was very slow.

mustKnowChunks.use: 원급 비교(as + 형용사 + as) 구문입니다.
mustKnowChunks.example: The initial battery was as large as a brick.

sentences.mustKnowGrammar: 등이접속사 'and'로 연결된 두 개의 독립절이며, 'as + 형용사(large) + as' 동등 비교 구문이 크기를 강조합니다.
sentences.feynmanExplanation: 옛날 벽돌 같은 핸드폰 시절에는 SIM 카드도 지갑에 넣는 신용카드만 한 엄청 커다란 플라스틱 판이었어요!

teachingTranscript.english: 'As large as credit cards' shows how technology shrunk.
teachingTranscript.korean: 'As large as credit cards'는 기술이 얼마나 축소되었는지를 보여줍니다.

sentences.original: However, SIM cards made mobile phones much more flexible.
sentences.chunkReading: However, / SIM cards made / mobile phones / much more flexible.
sentences.directKorean: 그러나, / SIM 카드는 만들었다 / 휴대전화를 / 훨씬 더 유연하게.
sentences.naturalKorean: 하지만 SIM 카드는 휴대전화를 훨씬 더 유연하고 편리하게 만들어 주었습니다.

mustKnowChunks.meaning: 훨씬 더 유연한, 훨씬 더 자유로운
mustKnowChunks.use: 비교급 강조 부사 much + 비교급(more flexible) 구문입니다.
mustKnowChunks.example: The new system is much more flexible.

sentences.mustKnowGrammar: 역접 접속어구 'However' 뒤에 5형식 동사 'make + 목적어(mobile phones) + 목적보어(much more flexible)' 구문이 왔으며, 'much'가 비교급을 강조합니다.
sentences.feynmanExplanation: 크기는 컸지만 SIM 카드 덕분에 기기를 바꿔도 전화번호를 그대로 유지할 수 있는 엄청난 편리함이 생겼지요.

teachingTranscript.english: 'Much' emphasizes the comparative adjective 'more flexible'.
teachingTranscript.korean: 'Much'는 비교급 형용사 'more flexible'을 강조합니다.

sentences.original: For the first time, users could move their personal phone number and network subscription from one device to another simply by swapping the small card.
sentences.chunkReading: For the first time, / users could move / their personal phone number / and network subscription / from one device to another / simply by swapping the small card.
sentences.directKorean: 처음으로, / 사용자들은 이동시킬 수 있었다 / 그들의 개인 전화번호를 / 그리고 네트워크 가입 정보를 / 한 기기에서 다른 기기로 / 단순히 그 작은 카드를 교체함으로써.
sentences.naturalKorean: 처음으로 사용자들은 그 작은 카드를 꼽아 바꾸는 것만으로 자신의 전화번호와 통신 가입 정보를 한 기기에서 다른 기기로 쉽게 옮길 수 있게 되었습니다.

mustKnowChunks.use: 역사적 최초의 사건을 강조할 때 씁니다.
mustKnowChunks.example: For the first time, people could text wirelessly.

mustKnowChunks.use: by + 동명사 구문으로 방법 수단을 나타냅니다.
mustKnowChunks.example: You can fix it simply by swapping batteries.

sentences.mustKnowGrammar: 부사구 'For the first time', 전치사구 'from one device to another', 그리고 수단 부사구 'by + 동명사(swapping)'가 사용되었습니다.
sentences.feynmanExplanation: 핸드폰을 새로 사도 칩만 빼서 새 핸드폰에 쏙 넣으면 내 번호 그대로 사용할 수 있게 된 거예요.

teachingTranscript.english: Notice 'from one device to another' showing mobility.
teachingTranscript.korean: 이동성을 보여주는 'from one device to another'에 주목하세요.

sentences.original: Inside every SIM card is a tiny computer chip that stores a unique identification number.
sentences.chunkReading: Inside every SIM card / is a tiny computer chip / that stores a unique identification number.
sentences.directKorean: 모든 SIM 카드 내부에는 / 아주 작은 컴퓨터 칩이 있다 / 고유한 식별 번호를 저장하는.
sentences.naturalKorean: 모든 SIM 카드 내부에는 고유한 식별 번호를 저장하는 아주 작은 컴퓨터 칩이 들어있습니다.

mustKnowChunks.use: 장소 전치사구가 문두에 오며 도치를 일으킵니다.
mustKnowChunks.example: Inside every phone is a powerful battery.

mustKnowChunks.use: 중복되지 않는 유일한 ID 번호를 뜻합니다.
mustKnowChunks.example: Each card has a unique identification number.

sentences.mustKnowGrammar: 장소 부사구(Inside every...)가 문두에 와서 주어(a tiny computer chip)와 동사(is)가 도치되었으며, 주격 관계대명사 'that'이 칩을 수식합니다.
sentences.feynmanExplanation: 작은 카드 속 반도체 칩 안에 전 세계에서 단 하나뿐인 나만의 신분증 번호가 저장되어 있어요.

teachingTranscript.english: This sentence uses location inversion: 'Inside every SIM card is...'
teachingTranscript.korean: 이 문장은 장소 도치 구문을 사용합니다: 'Inside every SIM card is...'

sentences.original: First, when you put a SIM card into your device and turn it on, the card communicates with a nearby mobile network tower.
sentences.chunkReading: First, / when you put a SIM card into your device / and turn it on, / the card communicates / with a nearby mobile network tower.
sentences.directKorean: 첫째로, / 당신이 SIM 카드를 기기에 넣고 / 전원을 켤 때, / 그 카드는 통신한다 / 근처의 이동 통신 기지국과.
sentences.naturalKorean: 첫째, SIM 카드를 기기에 넣고 전원을 켜면 카드가 근처의 이동 통신 기지국과 통신을 시작합니다.

mustKnowChunks.use: put A into B 구문입니다.
mustKnowChunks.example: Put the key into the lock.

mustKnowChunks.use: 무선 신호를 주고받는 기지국 탑을 뜻합니다.
mustKnowChunks.example: The signal comes from a nearby mobile network tower.

sentences.mustKnowGrammar: 순서 접속어 'First'로 프로세스 단계를 시작하며, 시간 부사절 접속사 'when'절 내에 두 동사(put, turn on)가 병렬 연결되어 있습니다.
sentences.feynmanExplanation: 1단계: 핸드폰을 켜면 SIM 카드가 주변에 있는 통신사 안테나(기지국) 신호를 찌르며 인사를 건네요.

teachingTranscript.english: 'First' marks step 1 in the process explanation.
teachingTranscript.korean: 'First'는 프로세스 설명의 1단계를 나타냅니다.

sentences.original: Next, the SIM card sends its special ID number to the network, essentially saying, 'Hey, it's me!'
sentences.chunkReading: Next, / the SIM card sends / its special ID number / to the network, / essentially saying, / 'Hey, it's me!'
sentences.directKorean: 다음으로, / SIM 카드는 전송한다 / 그것의 특별한 ID 번호를 / 네트워크로, / 본질적으로 말하면서, / '야, 나야!'라고.
sentences.naturalKorean: 다음으로 SIM 카드는 네트워크에 고유 ID 번호를 보내며 사실상 '저 왔어요, 나예요!'라고 신호를 보냅니다.

mustKnowChunks.use: send A to B 구문입니다.
mustKnowChunks.example: The card sends its special ID number to the server.

mustKnowChunks.use: 현재분사구문으로 비유적인 신호 의미를 쉽게 풀어 설명합니다.
mustKnowChunks.example: He nodded, essentially saying yes.

sentences.mustKnowGrammar: 순서 접속어 'Next'가 2단계를 도입하고, 3형식 문장 뒤에 의인화된 현재분사구문(essentially saying...)이 뒤따릅니다.
sentences.feynmanExplanation: 2단계: '저 OO통신사 손님 홍길동이에요!' 하고 암호 ID 번호를 기지국으로 쏩니다.

teachingTranscript.english: 'Next' signals step 2 of the connection process.
teachingTranscript.korean: 'Next'는 연결 프로세스의 2단계를 나타냅니다.

sentences.original: Then, the network verifies your account information, including your phone number and data plan.
sentences.chunkReading: Then, / the network verifies / your account information, / including your phone number / and data plan.
sentences.directKorean: 그러고 나서, / 네트워크는 확인한다 / 당신의 계정 정보를, / 당신의 전화번호를 포함하여 / 그리고 데이터 요금제를.
sentences.naturalKorean: 그러고 나면 네트워크는 여러분의 전화번호와 데이터 요금제를 포함한 계정 정보를 확인합니다.

mustKnowChunks.use: 데이터의 정당성을 체크함을 의미합니다.
mustKnowChunks.example: The computer verifies your account information.

mustKnowChunks.use: 통신사와 계약한 월간 데이터 이용 상품입니다.
mustKnowChunks.example: Unlimited data plan is popular.

sentences.mustKnowGrammar: 순서 접속어 'Then'이 3단계를 이끌며, 전치사 'including'이 세부 항목들을 예시로 나열합니다.
sentences.feynmanExplanation: 3단계: 통신사 컴퓨터가 '어, 홍길동 고객님 맞네! 요금 잘 냈고 데이터 10기가 남았네!' 하고 확인해요.

teachingTranscript.english: 'Then' introduces step 3: network verification.
teachingTranscript.korean: 'Then'은 3단계인 네트워크 검증을 도입합니다.

sentences.original: Finally, once the network approves your ID, your phone is ready to make calls, send text messages, and go online when Wi-Fi is unavailable.
sentences.chunkReading: Finally, / once the network approves your ID, / your phone is ready / to make calls, / send text messages, / and go online / when Wi-Fi is unavailable.
sentences.directKorean: 마침내, / 일단 네트워크가 당신의 ID를 승인하면, / 당신의 전화기는 준비된다 / 전화를 걸고, / 문자 메시지를 보내고, / 인터넷에 접속할 / 와이파이를 사용할 수 없을 때.
sentences.naturalKorean: 마침내 네트워크가 여러분의 ID를 승인하면, 와이파이를 쓸 수 없을 때도 전화기가 통화, 문자, 인터넷을 사용할 준비를 마칩니다.

mustKnowChunks.use: 접속사 once(~하자마자, 일단 ~하면) 구문입니다.
mustKnowChunks.example: Once you pass the test, you get the certificate.

mustKnowChunks.use: be ready + to부정사 구문입니다.
mustKnowChunks.example: The device is ready to connect.

sentences.mustKnowGrammar: 최종 접속어 'Finally'와 접속사 'once'절, 그리고 'be ready + to부정사' 병렬 구조(to make..., send..., and go...)가 사용되었습니다.
sentences.feynmanExplanation: 4단계: 승인이 끝나면 화면 상단에 안테나 칸이 뜨면서 전화, 문자, LTE/5G 인터넷이 팡팡 터지게 됩니다!

teachingTranscript.english: 'Finally' completes the 4-step process explanation.
teachingTranscript.korean: 'Finally'는 4단계 프로세스 설명을 완성합니다.

sentences.original: Over the past three decades, SIM cards have evolved dramatically.
sentences.chunkReading: Over the past three decades, / SIM cards / have evolved dramatically.
sentences.directKorean: 지난 30년 동안, / SIM 카드는 / 극적으로 진화해 왔다.
sentences.naturalKorean: 지난 30년 동안 SIM 카드는 극적으로 진화해 왔습니다.

mustKnowChunks.use: 30년(3 decades)에 걸친 지속적인 기간을 표현합니다.
mustKnowChunks.example: Technology changed over the past three decades.

mustKnowChunks.use: 현재완료 + 부사 구문으로 커다란 변화 과정을 나타냅니다.
mustKnowChunks.example: Smartphones have evolved dramatically.

sentences.mustKnowGrammar: 기간 부사구 'Over the past...'와 현재완료 동사구 'have evolved'가 쓰여 지속적인 변화를 설명합니다.
sentences.feynmanExplanation: 초창기 신용카드 크기에서 시작해 지금은 어떻게 변했을까요?

teachingTranscript.english: Notice 'have evolved dramatically' starting the modern trend paragraph.
teachingTranscript.korean: 최신 트렌드 단락을 시작하는 'have evolved dramatically'에 주목하세요.

sentences.original: As mobile devices became slimmer, physical SIM cards shrank from credit-card size to mini SIMs, micro SIMs, and nano SIMs.
sentences.chunkReading: As mobile devices became slimmer, / physical SIM cards shrank / from credit-card size / to mini SIMs, micro SIMs, and nano SIMs.
sentences.directKorean: 모바일 기기가 더 얇아짐에 따라, / 실물 SIM 카드는 줄어들었다 / 신용카드 크기에서 / 미니 SIM, 마이크로 SIM, 그리고 나노 SIM으로.
sentences.naturalKorean: 모바일 기기가 더욱 얇아짐에 따라 실물 SIM 카드는 신용카드 크기에서 미니 SIM, 마이크로 SIM, 나노 SIM으로 점점 작아졌습니다.

mustKnowChunks.use: 비례 비유 접속사 as(~함에 따라) 구문입니다.
mustKnowChunks.example: As time passed, things got better.

mustKnowChunks.use: shrink(과거 shrank) + from A to B 구문입니다.
mustKnowChunks.example: The chip shrank from large to micro size.

sentences.mustKnowGrammar: 접속사 'As'가 이끄는 부사절과 주절의 과거동사 'shrank', 그리고 'from A to B' 변화 구문이 사용되었습니다.
sentences.feynmanExplanation: 핸드폰이 얇아지면서 SIM 카단도 미니, 마이크로, 그리고 요즘 쓰는 손톱만 한 나노 SIM으로 점점 줄어들었어요.

teachingTranscript.english: Notice the size progression: mini, micro, nano.
teachingTranscript.korean: 크기의 감소 단계를 확인하세요: 미니, 마이크로, 나노.

sentences.original: Today, many modern smartphones use an eSIM, or embedded SIM, which is built directly inside the phone's circuit board.
sentences.chunkReading: Today, / many modern smartphones use / an eSIM, or embedded SIM, / which is built directly / inside the phone's circuit board.
sentences.directKorean: 오늘날, / 많은 현대 스마트폰은 사용한다 / eSIM, 즉 내장형 SIM을, / 그것은 직접 만들어져 내장되어 있다 / 스마트폰의 회로 기판 내부에서.
sentences.naturalKorean: 오늘날 많은 최신 스마트폰은 스마트폰의 회로 기판 내부에 직접 내장된 'eSIM(내장형 SIM)'을 사용합니다.

mustKnowChunks.meaning: 내장형 SIM, 칩 자체에 매립된 SIM
mustKnowChunks.use: embedded는 물체 내부에 고정 내장되었음을 뜻합니다.
mustKnowChunks.example: An embedded SIM does not need a tray.

mustKnowChunks.use: 부품이 외부에 노출되지 않고 기기 안에 들어있음을 뜻합니다.
mustKnowChunks.example: The battery is built directly inside.

sentences.mustKnowGrammar: 동격의 'or'를 통한 풀이(an eSIM, or embedded SIM)와 계속적 용법의 관계대명사 주격 'which is built...'가 부연 설명을 제공합니다.
sentences.feynmanExplanation: eSIM은 '플라스틱 조각'이 아니라 핸드폰 기판 안에 아예 내장되어 태어나는 디지털 칩이에요.

teachingTranscript.english: 'Embedded' means permanently placed inside.
teachingTranscript.korean: 'Embedded'는 영구적으로 내부에 위치한다는 의미입니다.

sentences.original: With an eSIM, users can download their network information digitally and switch mobile plans without swapping a physical plastic card.
sentences.chunkReading: With an eSIM, / users can download / their network information digitally / and switch mobile plans / without swapping a physical plastic card.
sentences.directKorean: eSIM을 사용하면, / 사용자들은 다운로드할 수 있다 / 그들의 네트워크 정보를 디지털로 / 그리고 모바일 요금제를 전환할 수 있다 / 실물 플라스틱 카드를 교체하지 않고도.
sentences.naturalKorean: eSIM을 이용하면 사용자들은 실물 플라스틱 카드를 바꿔 끼우지 않고도 디지털로 네트워크 정보를 다운로드하고 통신 요금제를 바꿀 수 있습니다.

mustKnowChunks.use: 무선 데이터 수신을 통한 프로필 설치를 의미합니다.
mustKnowChunks.example: You can download network information digitally in seconds.

mustKnowChunks.use: without + 동명사 구문입니다.
mustKnowChunks.example: You can change plans without swapping cards.

sentences.mustKnowGrammar: 전치사구 'With an eSIM' 뒤에 조동사 'can'에 걸리는 두 동사(download, switch)가 병렬 연결되고 'without + 동명사'가 결합되어 있습니다.
sentences.feynmanExplanation: eSIM을 쓰면 핀으로 구멍을 찔러 카드를 빼낼 필요 없이, QR코드나 앱 클릭으로 통신사를 바꿀 수 있어요!

teachingTranscript.english: Highlight the modern benefit of eSIMs: no physical swapping.
teachingTranscript.korean: eSIM의 현대적 장점인 '실물 교체 없음'을 강조하세요.

sentences.original: Today, billions of SIM cards are active around the world, connecting not only smartphones, but also smartwatches, tablets, and even connected cars to mobile networks.
sentences.chunkReading: Today, / billions of SIM cards / are active around the world, / connecting not only smartphones, / but also smartwatches, tablets, / and even connected cars / to mobile networks.
sentences.directKorean: 오늘날, / 수십억 개의 SIM 카드가 / 전 세계에서 활성화되어 있다, / 스마트폰뿐만 아니라, / 스마트워치, 태블릿, / 그리고 연결된 자동차까지 연결하면서 / 이동 통신망에.
sentences.naturalKorean: 오늘날 전 세계에서 수십억 개의 SIM 카드가 활성화되어 스마트폰뿐만 아니라 스마트워치, 태블릿, 그리고 커넥티드 카까지 이동 통신망에 연결해 주고 있습니다.

mustKnowChunks.use: billions of + 복수명사로 엄청난 수량을 표현합니다.
mustKnowChunks.example: Billions of devices are connected worldwide.

mustKnowChunks.chunk: not only A but also B
mustKnowChunks.use: 상관접속사 구문으로 대상을 확장할 때 씁니다.
mustKnowChunks.example: It connects not only phones but also watches.

sentences.mustKnowGrammar: 주어 'billions of SIM cards'와 현재분사구문 'connecting...', 그리고 상관접속사 'not only A, but also B'가 나열된 풍부한 결론 문장입니다.
sentences.feynmanExplanation: 핸드폰뿐 아니라 애플워치, 태블릿, 자동차의 네비게이션도 다 SIM 카드 덕분에 통신망에 연결되어 일하고 있답니다.

teachingTranscript.english: Conclude by mentioning the vast range of devices using SIM technology.
teachingTranscript.korean: SIM 기술을 사용하는 다양한 기기 범위를 언급하며 마무리하세요.

sentenceFrames: A SIM card helps a phone connect to a mobile network by __________.
A SIM card is a small chip that __________.
First, when you put the SIM card into the phone, __________.
Next, the SIM card tells the mobile network __________.
Today, eSIMs make this even easier because __________.
paragraphOutline: 1. Topic Sentence: State how a SIM card helps a phone connect to a mobile network.
2. Definition & Analogy: Briefly define a SIM card (small chip, ID number, name tag/bus pass).
3. Step-by-Step Process: Use process words (first, next, then, after that) to explain inserting card, sending ID, network checking account info, and opening access.
4. Modern Evolution: Mention how physical swapping evolved into eSIMs.
5. Concluding Sentence: End with a clear summary sentence wrapping up your explanation.

commonMistakes.mistake: First, put SIM card into phone and it connect network.
commonMistakes.correction: First, when you put the SIM card into the phone, it communicates with the network. (Use complete clauses and correct verb forms: 'communicates').

commonMistakes.mistake: Without SIM card, phone cannot make calls because it don't know network.
commonMistakes.correction: Without a SIM card, a phone cannot make calls because it does not know which network to join. (Ensure subject-verb agreement: 'it does not know').

teacherCorrectionFocus: Check that students write between 100–140 words.
Ensure students describe the step-by-step process clearly using target process connectors (first, next, then, after that, finally).
Verify that students cite text details (e.g. ID number, account info, phone number/plan, eSIM).
